frequency_question: What proportion of major standalone bills introduced and prioritized in the U.S. Senate complete committee referral, floor scheduling, debate, amendments, and final passage within a single 285-day legislative session window?
membership_rule: Includes all major federal statutory bills that reached a floor vote in the U.S. Senate over the past three congressional sessions; excludes routine unanimous consent resolutions, judicial confirmations, and must-pass omnibus appropriations bills.
provenance_note: 7 cases named, 12 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.7x)
coverage_note: 12 named major standalone policy bills tracked across two recent congressional sessions; believed roughly 20 total attempted standalone priorities in that window.
known_gaps: Excludes minor technical corrections bills and unvoted committee measures.
skeleton: Legislative sessions divided into 2-year congresses, examining the subset of prioritized partisan/bipartisan policy bills that successfully navigate the sequential timeline of committee consideration, cloture motions, and final roll call within calendar constraints.
multiplier: 7 hits out of 12 major prioritized standalone bills evaluated across recent sessions = ~58%
validity_reason: Base rate remains stable across the duration of the current and immediate next congressional terms under standard Senate standing rules.
